newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Gold seen diving to new lows, no support in sight.
newsitem.headline: Gold seen diving to new lows, no support in sight.

text.p: Gold prices look set to get a further hammering and may dive to a fresh low of US$360 an ounce over the next few days, Singapore-based precious metal dealers said on Tuesday.

Producer selling by South African and Australian mining companies, fund managers liquidating their positions before the Christmas holiday period and a shift in funds to booming stock markets from Hong Kong to Wall Street pounded gold, they said.
"It may come down to even $360 an ounce. For the short-term, there's really no upside for gold," a bank trader said.

"All the money has gone to Wall Street and bourses like the Hang Seng (in Hong Kong). Some funds also found its way into the strong (U.S.) dollar. There's not a whole lot of money left for gold," a trader said.

Spot gold was trading in Hong Kong around $367.90 an ounce at 0310 GMT on Tuesday, its lowest level since April 1994, and down from $368/$368.50 in late trade in New York on Monday. Gold was trading a few weeks ago at around $380 an ounce.
The situation has been aggravated by the drying up of already scanty physical buying in Asia, traders said.
Jewellers said buyers dropped out of the market on expectations that prices of the yellow metal will slide further.
"Very few people are buying gold. There's only very scattered buying in Asia," one Singapore-based gold jeweller said.
"Unless strong buying comes back to the market, you will not see a rebound in gold prices," one dealer said.
